HEMATOLOGY CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Hematopathology and Molecular Diagnostics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Referral Reason: Macrocytic anemia with thrombocytosis, refractory to conventional treatment
Clinical History: Patient presents with persistent macrocytic anemia (MCV 108 fL) and thrombocytosis (platelets 580 x 10^9/L). Previous treatment with vitamin B12 and folate supplementation showed no improvement. No significant family history of hematological malignancies reported.

TEST PERFORMED
Conventional Cytogenetics - G-banded Karyotype Analysis

METHODOLOGY
Bone marrow aspirate cells were cultured for 24 and 48 hours without mitogens. Metaphase chromosomes were G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa technique. Twenty metaphases were analyzed at 400-550 band resolution. Karyotypes were described according to the International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature (ISCN 2020).

RESULTS

KARYOTYPE: 46,XX,del(5)(q13q33)[15]/46,XX[5]

ABNORMAL CLONE: 15 of 20 metaphases (75%) showed an interstitial deletion of the long arm of chromosome 5
Deletion breakpoints: 5q13 to 5q33
NORMAL CLONE: 5 of 20 metaphases (25%) showed normal female karyotype

INTERPRETATION
The cytogenetic analysis reveals a clonal abnormality consisting of an interstitial deletion of chromosome 5q in 75% of analyzed cells. The deleted region spans from band q13 to q33, encompassing the commonly deleted region (CDR) associated with 5q- syndrome. This finding, in conjunction with the clinical presentation of macrocytic anemia and thrombocytosis, is highly consistent with myelodysplastic syndrome with isolated del(5q) (5q- syndrome).

The 5q deletion involves critical genes including RPS14 (ribosomal protein gene), SPARC, and multiple microRNA genes that contribute to the characteristic phenotype. The presence of this isolated cytogenetic abnormality without additional chromosomal aberrations is associated with a relatively favorable prognosis among MDS subtypes.

LINEAGE-SPECIFIC CONSIDERATIONS
The del(5q) abnormality particularly affects erythroid development, leading to the characteristic macrocytic anemia. The paradoxical thrombocytosis observed in 5q- syndrome is thought to result from haploinsufficiency of specific genes within the deleted region that normally regulate megakaryopoiesis.

TREATMENT RESPONSE PREDICTION
Patients with isolated del(5q) typically show excellent response to lenalidomide therapy, with high rates of transfusion independence and cytogenetic remission. The absence of additional cytogenetic abnormalities supports a favorable treatment response profile.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Consider initiation of lenalidomide therapy as first-line treatment for 5q- syndrome
2. Monitor complete blood counts monthly during treatment initiation
3. Perform follow-up cytogenetic analysis at 3-6 months to assess treatment response
4. Evaluate patient for allogeneic stem cell transplant candidacy, particularly if <65 years old
5. Screen for TP53 mutations, as their presence may impact prognosis and treatment decisions
6. Monitor for disease progression with serial bone marrow evaluations

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Reviewed by: [redacted name], MD, Director of Cytogenetics Laboratory
